avatar.$exception: Avatar initials use line-height equal to font-size — required for vertical centering within a fixed circle. Sizes below caption preset (12px) are necessary at small avatar dimensions.

list-item.$note: Structural shell with three slots: leading (icon/avatar), content (consumer-driven), trailing (action/icon). Type comes from the body/{tier} ramp on the container, so it is inherited rather than imposed: a bare string scales with the row, and any child carrying its own text-* class still wins. Without it, size would move height, x-padding and gap while content held one size at every tier — a size ladder that does nothing to what you can read. The leading and trailing slots are deliberately unsized — they hold avatars and controls as well as icons, so a size-icon-* wrapper would constrain the non-icon cases.

accordion.$note: Collapsible section group. Header defines the toggle label — content area is a blank container for consumer-driven content. **This covers the single-panel case too**: `type="single" collapsible` with one AccordionItem is a disclosure panel, so the catalog has no separate single-panel component. A dedicated one would differ only in whether group state is carried — same surface, same trigger, same chevron — and carrying unused group state is cheaper than maintaining two components that render identically.

kbd.$note: Keyboard shortcut indicator. Inline element styled as a key cap. Platform-appropriate modifier keys (Cmd vs Ctrl) are code-only. Combination keys separated by + with gap between elements. min-width per size equals that size's own box height (y-padding × 2 + line-height + border × 2), so a single narrow character like p or an arrow glyph renders as a square cap rather than a pinched one — x-padding cannot do this, because it scales with the content instead of setting a floor.

sm.$exception: 2px y-padding — below spacing scale minimum. Required to maintain proportional key cap at small font size.

avatar-group.$note: Stacked avatars with overlap + a +N overflow counter. Composition over `avatar` — size forwards to children; overlap (negative margin) and the surface-colored ring are structural/frozen.

relative-time.$note: Relative timestamp ('2 hours ago') via Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. Client component — renders <time dateTime> with an SSR-stable date fallback, swaps to the relative string after mount (avoids server-now != client-now hydration mismatch). Optional `live` interval keeps it fresh. **No Figma card**: its only visual output is a formatted string, and a frame of four sample strings is sample copy rather than a specimen — nothing about it is a design decision a designer would make. The same bar applies to any atom whose output is a formatted string rather than an arrangement.
